repo.description:
### Summary

The public shared-view bulk endpoints iterated a caller-supplied filter array with no cap on its length, running a full data query for every element of an unauthenticated request.

### Details

The bulk data-list and bulk aggregate handlers in `public-datas.service.ts` walked the request's filter list and issued one complete data-list operation per entry, each carrying its own SQL execution and formula evaluation. Nothing bounded the array: in the Community Edition the public-API limiter guard on these routes admits every request unconditionally, and the JSON body parser accepts payloads up to 50MB, so a body of minimal filter objects a few dozen bytes each converted into on the order of a million database queries in a single request. Query cost grew linearly with array length, taking CPU time and resident memory with it.

### Impact

An attacker could exhaust CPU and memory and take the NocoDB process down with one POST request. No authentication is required - only the UUID of a shared view, which is the very value these links are meant to be distributed by and which routinely reaches search indexes and messaging apps.

### Credit

This issue was reported by [@pavanchow](https://github.com/pavanchow).
repo.summary: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption via Shared View Bulk API
